case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 16.05.2007 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 2431 & 2432 of 1994).
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. These two appeals, by leave, are directed against the judgment and order dated 16.5.2007, passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 2431 and 2432 of 1994 making the Rule issued in Civil Revision No.2431 of 1994 absolute in part and Rule issued in Civil Revision No.2432 of 1994 absolute.

2. Relevant facts leading to filing of these two Civil Appeals, in brief, are:

<u>3. That the present appellants (in both the appeals) and one Saleha Khatun instituted Title Suit No.31 of 1991 in the 2nd Court of Assistant Judge, Barisal, (originally Title Suit No. 224 of 1985 in the 1st Court of the then Munsif, Barisal) seeking declaration that the auction sale of the suit land as mentioned in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint in Certificate Case No. 472(KT)/1983-84 is fraudulent, collusive, illegal and not binding upon them. On the other hand, the present respondent Nos. 1 and 2 also instituted Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 in the 2nd Court of Assistant Judge, Barisal, (originally Title Suit No. 241 of 1985 in the First Court of the then Munsif, Barisal) against the present appellants and proforma respondent Nos.3-14 (in both the appeals) as defendants, seeking declaration of their title in the suit land and for further declaration that the decree dated 10.8.1959 passed in Title Suit No.220 of 1959 of the 2nd Court of Munsif, Barisal is fraudulent, illegal and not binding upon them.</u>

4. It is stated in the plaint of Title Suit No. 31 of 1991 that the suit land originally belonged to Amorendra Nath and others who settled the same with one Abdus Sobahan and Abdul Hamid Howlader; that the said Abdus Sobahan died leaving behind his only son, the plaintiff No.1 and Abdul Hamid Howlader died leaving behind plaintiff Nos.2 to 5 as heirs. It is alleged that when the suit land was wrongly recorded in SA Khatian they instituted Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 and obtained a compromise decree on 10.8.1959, on the basis of which the plaintiffs got the suit land recorded in their names and since then they have been possessing the same. It is further alleged that the defendants fraudulently created an auction sale proceeding in respect of the suit land in Certificate Case No. 472 (KT)/83-84 but did not acquire any title or possession in the same. Hence, the suit.

5. On the other hand, the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 (the present respondent Nos. 1 & 2) in their plaint stated that the suit land belonged to Amorendra Nath and others and the same was put in auction in Certificate Case No. 472(KT)/83-84 and defendant Nos.13 to 16 purchased the same; that the sale was confirmed and the auction purchasers were given possession of the same. The plaintiffs (present respondent Nos.1 and 2) purchased the suit land from the auction purchasers by registered kabala dated 11.4.1985 and have been in possession of the same since then. It is further alleged that the defendants (plaintiffs of Title Suit No.31 of 1991) instituted false Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 and obtained a forged and collusive compromise decree on 10.8.1959 by practicing fraud upon the court. Hence, Title suit No. 224 of 1985 (original Title suit No.31 of 1991) should be dismissed and Title suit No. 241 of 1985 (original Title suit No. 35 of 1991) should be decreed.

6. The defendants of both the suits contested the above suits by filing their respective written statements denying the claims of each other and relied upon the statements made in their respective plaints.

7. The learned Assistant Judge, after hearing both the suits analogously, dismissed both the suits by judgment and decree dated 19.02.1992. Then the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 (present respondent Nos. 1 and 2) preferred Title Appeal No. 53 of 1992 and the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.31 of 1981 (present appellants) preferred Title Appeal No.135 of 1992. The learned Subordinate Judge (Now Joint District Judge) after hearing both the appeals analogously, allowed Title Appeal No. 135 of 1992 and thereby decreed Title Suit No. 31 of 1991 and dismissed Title Appeal No. 53 of 1992 and thereby affirmed the dismissal of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 by judgment and decree dated 27.4.1994. As against that, the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 (present respondents) moved the High Court Division and obtained two Rules in Civil Revision Nos. 2431 and 2432 of 1994.

8. The High Court Division after hearing both the parties, made the Rule issued in Civil Revision No. 2432 of 1994 absolute and thereby dismissed Title, Suit No. 31 of 1991 filed by the present appellants and made the Rule issued in Civil Revision 2431 of 1994 absolute in part and thereby decreed Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 (filed by the present respondent Nos. 1 and 2) in part declaring only to the extent that the judgment and decree dated 10.08.1959 passed in Title suit No. 220 of 1959 is illegal, void and not binding upon the present respondents, by the impugned judgment and order dated 16.5.2007.

9. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order dated 16.5.2007, passed in Civil Revision Nos. 2431 of 1994 and 2432 of 1994, the present appellants moved this Court in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.1618 of 2007 and 1619 of 2007 and obtained leave giving rise to the instant two appeals.

10. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants of both the appeals submits that the respondents filed title suit No.35 of 1985 praying for declaration of title to the land mentioned it schedule 'ka' to the plaint on the basis of auction purchase and also praying for a declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 as illegal and void and the trial court after having found the alleged auction purchase fraudulent and void dismissed the suit and the said judgment and decree of the trial court was affirmed by the appellate court. But the High Court Division affirmed the judgment of two lower courts regarding acquisition of title by that alleged auction purchase but committed error in passing part decree so far it relates to the validity of Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 without considering the fact that since the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 failed to establish their title to the suit property they have no locus standi to challenge the decree obtained by the plaintiffs in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959. He further submits that the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.31 of 1991(i.e. the present appellants) filed the suit in respect of 1.40 acres of land of Plot No. 21 and .85 acre of land of Plot No.3 on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959, the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991(i.e. the respondent Nos. 1 and 2) herein, filed their suit in respect of 1.40 acres of land of Plot No. 21 only, but the High Court Division committed error in passing a part decree in favour of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 in respect of entire suit land of Title Suit No.31 of 1991.So the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.

11. Mr. Abdul Quiyum, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that the lower appellate court did not reverse the finding of the trial court as regards fraud in respect of the disputed decree of Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 but reversed the judgment of the trial court relying upon the Bank of Calcutta Ltd. vs. Debendra Nath Singh and others reported in 19 DLR 400, which is not applicable in this case. He also submits that the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 31 of 1991 (the present appellants) have no locus standi to challenge the auction of the defendants as the so called settlement in 1358 BS, which is the basis of their title, is not proved by them. He further submits that the courts below misconstrued the evidence of PW-1 who proved mutation by the defendant respondents after the auction purchase within the knowledge of the plaintiffs, so the auction was not fraudulent and as a result the appellants are not entitled to get decree as prayed for.

<u>12. On consideration of the submissions advanced on behalf of both the parties and on perusal of the impugned judgment and order and the materials on record it appears that, admittedly, the suit land belonged to Amarendra Nath and others. The plaintiffs of Title Suit No.31 of 20,09, (hereinafter mentioned as appellants claimed that Abdus Subhan Mia, (the plaintiff appellant No. l) and Abdul Hamid Hawlader (predecessor of Plaintiff appellant Nos. 2 to 6) took settlement of the suit land from Amarendra Nath and others; but they did not disclose the date or year of such settlement in their plaint. PW-1, Abdus Sobhan Miah, in his deposition stated that they took settlement from Baidhyanath in the year 1358 BS; but no other PW corroborated PW-1 in this respect nor has the settlement been proved by producing either Patta or Kabuliyat or any other written document. Under the Bengal Tenancy Act, though settlement may be granted orally without any written instrument but in case, if any question arose as to genuineness of such settlement then burden always lies upon the person claiming as such to prove the same settlement by proper oral evidence. But in the present case the appellants have failed to prove such settlement by any proper evidence either oral or documentary. Thus when the settlement, the basis of appellants title, is not proved by proper evidence, they cannot claim title through auction purchase.</u>

13. The learned advocate for the appellants claimed that the suit land was not recorded in the names of the settlement holders in the SA Khatian and as a result they filed Title suit No. 220 of 1959 and obtained a compromise decree and by that decree the appellants made the record corrected and thereby included their names in the record and relying upon such submission the appellate court decreed Title Suit No. 31 of 1991 only on the basis of the said compromise decree [Exhibit-2(ka)] passed on 10.8.1959. But on examination of the plaint of Title Suit No. 220 of 1959, the solenama (Exhibit-2) and the Sole decree [Exhibit-2(Ka)] it transpires that there were two plaintiffs and seven defendants in the said suit but none other than Amarendranath (one defendant) and the sole plaintiff No.1, Abdul Hamed, signed the said solenama and the plaintiff No.1 alone put his signature at the bottom of the same. Interestingly neither the other six defendants nor the plaintiff No. 2, Abdul Subhan Miah, signed the said solenama. Moreover, the solenama was not proved by either party of the suit and there is no explanation as to why others did not sign that solenama. On the other hand PW-2, Subudh Chandra Majhi, in his cross examination admitted that “বাবুদের সহিত পত্তনের সময় কথা হইয়াছে যে, মোকদ্দমা করিলেই সোলে করিয়া দিবে। ঐ সময় অন্য বাবুরা বাড়িতেই ছিল।

<u>14. Moreover, it also appears that Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 was filed in 1959 and the same claimed to have been decreed on compromise on 10.8.1959 but the Vokalatnama of the said suit appears to have been accepted on 5.5.1985 which is illusive and rather creates doubt. It also appears that no notice was served upon the original owners of the suit land and the defendants of that suit did not appear in the court before signing the Solenama. That's why the trial court found the Vokalatnama of the said suit to be forged one. Again, on perusal of the sole decree [Exhibit-2(ka)] it appears that the suit was disposed of on compromise on 10.08.1959 bit the said decree appears to have been signed by the learned Judge on 19.08.1958. Thus, it is not clear how the decree was prepared and signed one year before passing of the same. These abundant discrepancies in the decree of Title Suit No.220 of 1959 clearly prove that the solenama was not only a fraudulent one but also collusive one and as a result such illegal decree cannot confer any title upon the appellants.</u>

<u>15. It appears that the trial court upon considering all these aspects rightly assessed the evidence and considered the materials on record and dismissed the suit but the lower appellate court without properly considering the evidence on record, simply relied upon the aforesaid compromise decree and allowed the appeal and decreed the suit which the High Court Division on consideration of materials on record found the orders of the court of appeal below not sustainable in the eye of law and as a result set aside the judgment and decree of the lower appellate court and affirmed those of the trial court.</u>

<u>16. On the other hand the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.35 of 1991 (hereinafter mentioned as present respondents) claimed that the suit land was put in auction in Certificate Case Nos. 472(KT)/1983-84 and 387(KT)/1976- 77which was purchased by defendant Nos. 1-3 and 5 who took possession of the same through court on 12.10.1984 and since then they have been possessing the same. Subsequently, on 11.04.1985 they transferred .85 acre of land out of the said auction purchased land to this respondent who was given possession of the same. But the courts below found that they failed to prove the sale certificate in support of such auction sale/purchase, also failed to prove delivery of possession and service of notice under sections 7 and 46 of the Public Demand Recovery Act. Though the plaintiffs of Title suit No. 220 of 1959 claimed that they purchased the same from the persons who purchased such land in auction they failed to prove that auction by producing proper evidence. DW-1, Abdur Rashid Khan, deposed that he got possession of the suit land in 1985 but DW-2, Sultan Howladar, admitted in his cross examination that ‘One Gobinda Babu possessed the suit land till 1991' Interestingly DW-4, Razni Kanta Baliar, in his cross examination stated that the plaintiffs (the present respondents) have been possessing the suit land for 20/21 years. On the other hand PW-5, Wazed Ali, in his cross examination stated that the plaintiffs (present respondents) have been possessing the suit land for about 14/15 years. From the aforesaid evidence and discussion it is abundantly clear that the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 have totally failed to prove their possession in the suit land.</u>

17. The learned Advocate for the appellants, on the face of the respondents' Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 for declaration of their title to the suit land on the basis of auction purchase in the year 1985 and also for a declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 is illegal and void submitted that since they failed to prove the auction purchase they cannot get a decree for declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 is illegal and void. It is true that the respondents filed their Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 for two declarations, one for declaration of title to the land described in schedule-I to the plaint and another for two declarations, one for declaration of title to the land described in schedule-I to the plaint and another for declaration that the decree passed in title suit No. 220 of 1959 is fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon them. These two prayers are separate and independent and they filed that suit by paying separate court fees for these two separate prayers. Though they filed to prove their title to the land described in schedule-I to the plaint they have successfully proved that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 is fraudulent, illegal and collusive.

So, they can get part decree to the extent of their second prayer. Hence, the High Court Division Committed no wrong in decreeing the suit in part to extent of declaring the decree passed in the Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 to be fraudulent, void, illegal and not binding upon them.

18. The appellants further claimed that they filed their Title Suit No. 31 of 1991 in respect of 2.25 acres of land in plot Nos. 21 and 3 but the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 in respect of 1.40 acres of land only in plot No. 21 along with a prayer for declaring the decree of Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 fraudulent and void etc. So, the decree passed by the High Court Division is not maintainable in the eye of law. It is required to mention here that though the respondents’ first prayer was in respect of 1.40 acres of land their second prayer for declaration was in respect of the whole suit land i.e. 2.25 acres of land including 1.40 acre of land described in schedule-1 which was the subject matter of Title Suit No. 220 of 1959. So, the claim of the learned Advocate for the appellants finds no legal ground in this respect.

19. So, the trial court and the lower appellate court after examining the evidence and materials on record rightly dis-missed both the suits to the extent to which the plaintiffs failed to prove and the High Court Division also rightly affirmed the judgment and order of those two lower courts. But, the High Court Division in its revisional jurisdiction rightly observed that the evidence on record clearly proved that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 was fraudulent and collusive and as a result the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.35 of 1991 can get part decree to that extent in that suit.

20. Thus the findings and decision arrived at by the High Court Division being based on proper appreciation of fact and law do not call for interference by this Division.

21. Accordingly, these two civil appeals are dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.
